messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: network: high error rates and stalled TCP flows in eu-west-3 (AZ5) affecting dual-stack LBs — alert threshold hit (5min). Incident created: INC-20250317-az5-ptm

oncall_sre_maya: I’m on it — acknowledging page. Is anyone already seeing customer reports?

support_lead_raj: multiple support tickets about page loads timing out; customers on native v6 appear hit hardest. Some report errors from services behind our regional LBs.

netops_jamie: quick summary from our NOC: starting ~09:02 UTC we saw a spike in ICMP fragmentation-needed and PMTUD failures across AZ5 transit. Many flows fall back or stall. Suspect MTU mismatch after recent infra change.

alice_prodeng: what infra change? Any recent host/kernel or cloud NIC config?

netops_jamie: ops change log: yesterday config push to enable jumbo frames on the AZ5 host NICs to optimize throughput for large model caches. Cloud provider docs said end-to-end must be configured but we only flipped on host side.

oncall_sre_maya: that would create blackhole for PMTUD where ICMP unreachable for DF=1 is blocked or drops. IPv6 prefers DF and PMTU path discovery. Symptoms match.

dns_admin_lina: interestingly, regional DNS ingress LB healthchecks are mostly v4, but app LBs accept v6 and are seeing session stalls. Could explain why some customers (v6 pref) fail while others ok.

oncall_sre_maya: can someone run a quick traceroute6/tracepath to a failing backend from an affected host? I want to confirm where ICMPv6 frag-needed is being dropped.

netops_jamie: running now from az5-bastion1: ```$ tracepath -n -6 2a01:xxxx::backend-ip
 1:  fe80::1(0.123ms)
 2:  2a01:xxxx::gw (0.8ms)
 3:  *
 4:  *
  pmtu: 1500
```

oncall_sre_maya: run `ping6 -c3 -M do -s 1400 <backend>` with DF set to test.

netops_jamie: ```$ ping6 -c3 -M do -s 1400 2a01:xxxx::backend
PING 2a01:xxxx::backend(2a01:xxxx::backend) 1400 data bytes
From 2a01:xxxx::gw icmp_seq=1 Frag needed and DF set
From 2a01:xxxx::gw icmp_seq=2 Frag needed and DF set
--- 2a01:xxxx::backend ping statistics ---
3 packets transmitted, 0 received, +2 errors, 100% packet loss, time 2022ms
```

oncall_sre_maya: confirms PMTUD messages are generated but not getting back or not processed properly. Two options: 1) revert jumbo frame enable on host NICs in AZ5 to 1500, or 2) apply MSS clamping at edge to force smaller MSS for TCP. For immediate mitigation I prefer clamping on our regional NAT/LB so we don't need host rollback.

alice_prodeng: MSS clamp change is lower risk. We can patch the frontend LB config to set TCP MSS to 1400 for ipv6 traffic. Any idea of control-plane window to push?

netops_jamie: platform team: can we apply an iptables/ip6tables rule or LB-level config? Cloud LB supports TCP options for IPv4 only in their UI; but their API supports connection-level TCP options for both. I can script via API now.

platform_pm_henry: approve emergency API call. Make sure to include a short TTL/rollback (20 mins) and monitor.

netops_jamie: doing it now. Script: ```curl -X POST https://provider.api/lbs/az5/update -d '{"tcp_mss":1400,"ipv6":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'```

incident-bot: deploy-bot published: lb-config/az5-tcp-mss-1400 @env=prod — run ID dbf7e1.

netops_jamie: applied MSS clamp at frontend LBs in AZ5 09:15 UTC. Rolling restart of connections happening. Observability: RTTs dropping, error counts decreasing.

support_lead_raj: I see support tickets updating — users report intermittent failures are resolving. Marking impacted tickets as mitigation in progress.

alice_prodeng: can we confirm no regressions for large payload workloads? Need to check model cache prefetch and streaming.

oncall_sre_maya: running synthetic checks across v6 and v4 clients now. Results: v6 latency stable, no packet loss; model streaming tests ok at 1200-1300 byte chunks. No obvious regression.

customer_tix_bot: auto-update: 42 open tickets suspected impacted — 30 updated to "mitigation applied".

dns_admin_lina: as a precaution, setting our control-plane to prefer IPv4 for healthchecks only in AZ5 so that cross-region DNS failover won't trigger incorrectly while we stabilize. Will revert after rollback.

netops_jamie: also pushed a temporary BGP community to avoid asymmetric path that may be blocking ICMPv6 fragments; this will remain for 30m.

oncall_sre_maya: good. Next steps: 1) keep MSS clamp for 30m while monitoring 2) plan host rollback of jumbo frames in AZ5 for tomorrow if we want jumbo — require coordinated end-to-end config 3) create postmortem owner 4) customer communication draft.

platform_pm_henry: I'll own the postmortem (PM). Add timeline and config diff. Please assign root-cause after full repro.

alice_prodeng: note for postmortem: this is a classic PMTUD + IPv6 preference interaction — IPv6 path discovery is fragile when middleboxes drop ICMPv6. We should add e2e check in canary that exercises DF and large MTU across regions.

oncall_sre_maya: agree. Also adding a checklist item: when enabling jumbo frames, ensure NIC, host OS, hypervisor, and network fabric are toggled in same maintenance window and tested with large-packet e2e tests.

incident-bot: incident INC-20250317-az5-ptm status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to SEV3.

support_lead_raj: drafting customer advisory: "Intermittent connectivity for IPv6 clients in eu-west-3 (AZ5) due to PMTUD failures after NIC MTU change; mitigation applied. We will follow up with a technical postmortem."

netops_jamie: monitoring graphs: errors back to baseline at 09:28 UTC. Continuing to watch.

oncall_sre_maya: handing over to night on-call @oncall_sre_jun for observation window. Handoff notes: MSS clamp in place (1400) on AZ5 LBs, BGP community temporary, host jumbo frames rolled back on 3 hosts so far — will finish overnight if stable. Postmortem owner: platform_pm_henry.

oncall_sre_maya: I’m moving to post-incident activities. If anything spikes, page SRE.

oncall_sre_jun: acknowledged. I’ll monitor next 6 hours.

incident-bot: incident INC-20250317-az5-ptm assigned to platform_pm_henry for postmortem.

platform_pm_henry: thanks — I’ll put together timeline and follow-up actions. Expect initial draft within 24h.

support_lead_raj: closing loop with customers and tagging their tickets.

alice_prodeng: recommend we add an automated test: `sudo ping6 -M do -s 1400` from new host templates to ensure MTU path is traversable during canaries.

netops_jamie: created follow-up ticket: NET-794: "AZ5 jumbo frames rollback + PMTUD e2e test" and assigned to netops.

incident-bot: incident INC-20250317-az5-ptm is now in MONITORING.

oncall_sre_maya: final note: root cause (provisional): host NIC jumbo frames enabled without coordinated fabric/config, causing PMTUD failures and ICMPv6 frag-needed messages being dropped. Mitigation: MSS clamp at LB + partial host rollback. Postmortem required.

customer_tix_bot: postmortem note queued: customers notified, tickets updated"
